problem_found: Wikipedia gives opening figures as free text in inconsistent forms (day vs weekend, worldwide vs India, ranges, USD)
action_taken: Saved all 38 candidate sentences; one verified phrase per film chosen in data/manual/first_weekend_phrases.csv
why: No single regex picks the right figure on every page; a human choice that the script verifies word-for-word against the source is transparent and cannot invent numbers

problem_found: Infobox has no Budget field for some films
action_taken: Kept films; budget left missing (NULL) for them
why: Budget is a confounder we describe, not our outcome — dropping films for it would shrink an already small n

problem_found: YouTube comment JSON contains author names, channel ids and profile URLs
action_taken: Dropped 5 identifying columns during flattening: authorDisplayName, authorProfileImageUrl, authorChannelUrl, authorChannelId, channelId
why: Brief's ground rule: protect people. Usernames never leave data/raw/, which is gitignored

problem_found: Channel search returned promo videos (launch events, speeches, Shorts, 30 s cut-downs) whose titles contain 'trailer'
action_taken: Kept only the main trailer plus videos with 'trailer' in the title, no promo words, and length within 10% of the main trailer
why: Dubbed language versions are the same edit, so same length; counting promos would inflate views for films with busy channels (Peddi had 16 'trailer' videos, 1 real)

problem_found: TMDb genres and cast are lists inside JSON, which do not fit in one table cell
action_taken: Joined genre names into one comma-separated text column; kept only top-3 billed cast
why: One row per film keeps the films table simple; we describe genre/cast, we don't model them

problem_found: Same film spelled differently across 5 sources (e.g. TMDb 'Kantara - A Legend: Chapter 1', YouTube 'RAID 2 (TRAILER): Ajay D | ...')
action_taken: Normalised titles (lowercase, removed brackets, 'trailer', language tags, text after '|', punctuation) then rapidfuzz-scored against the 10 canonical titles
why: A shared film_id is what lets us JOIN trailers, box office, comments and trends

problem_found: Fuzzy scores below 95
action_taken: 70–94: sent to a human (M9, data/manual/match_review.csv); below 70: rejected
why: A wrong join silently corrupts every later number, so uncertain matches are checked by a person

problem_found: Yearly grossing table row 'Dhurandhar' (the 2025 prequel) looks like 'Dhurandhar: The Revenge'
action_taken: Rejected by token_sort_ratio (extra words lower the score), not joined to any film
why: partial_ratio would have scored it 100 and joined the wrong film's ₹1,350 crore gross

problem_found: Budget given as text ranges (e.g. '₹90–130 crore[a]', 'est. ₹30−40 crore[3][4]') with footnotes and a Unicode minus sign
action_taken: Stripped footnotes/'est.', treated '–' and '−' as range dashes, took the midpoint in ₹ crore
why: A single number per film is needed for SQL and charts; the midpoint is the least biased point in a published range

problem_found: Budget missing (Kantara: Chapter 1) or shared with another film (Dhurandhar: The Revenge 'combined with part 1')
action_taken: Set budget_cr to NULL; films kept
why: Halving a combined budget would invent a number (1 combined); budget is a described confounder, not our outcome

problem_found: Running time differs between Wikipedia and TMDb
action_taken: Used Wikipedia's runtime (biggest gap 6 min); TMDb kept for comparison only
why: Wikipedia cites the censor-board certificate for most films; TMDb is user-edited. One rule for all films

problem_found: TMDb release date is 1 day earlier than Wikipedia for some films
action_taken: Used Wikipedia's theatrical release date
why: TMDb often records paid-preview / overseas dates; the screen decision is about the Indian theatrical opening

problem_found: Box-office figures published as ranges (e.g. '₹325–335 crore')
action_taken: Converted to the midpoint; low/high kept in the note column
why: Trade sources disagree; the midpoint avoids picking a side

problem_found: Dhurandhar: The Revenge first weekend only published in USD ('over $80 million')
action_taken: Converted at the ECB reference rate on its release date (₹93.25/USD, Frankfurter API) and noted it is a lower bound
why: Excluding it would lose the biggest film in the sample; converting at the release-date rate is reproducible and logged

problem_found: First weekends are 3 days (Friday release) for some films and 4 days (Thursday release) for others
action_taken: Added first_weekend_per_day = first-weekend gross ÷ number of days
why: Comparing a 4-day total with a 3-day total would favour Thursday releases by about a third

problem_found: Two weekend figures are not clearly worldwide (Housefull 5 domestic only; Sitaare Zameen Par scope not stated)
action_taken: Kept, flagged in the note column, and tested with/without them in the analysis
why: Dropping them leaves n = 8; keeping them flagged lets us show whether they change the result

problem_found: Lifetime gross appears in two Wikipedia places (film infobox and the yearly list)
action_taken: Kept both with their source; largest disagreement 0.6%
why: Two independent-looking tables that agree within a few % raises confidence in the figures

problem_found: YouTube counts arrive as text and timestamps as ISO-8601 UTC strings
action_taken: Counts → integers (hidden likes stay NULL, not 0); timestamps → IST datetimes
why: Text sorts '9' after '81728371'; UTC would put late-evening IST trailers on the wrong day

problem_found: Same comment id downloaded twice (pages shift while new comments arrive during paging)
action_taken: Dropped repeats, kept first
why: A comment counted twice would inflate velocity and that film's sentiment weight

problem_found: Comments contain URLs (links, timestamps to other videos)
action_taken: Removed URLs from text, kept the rest of the comment
why: URLs carry no sentiment and distort length and term counts

problem_found: Empty comments after cleaning (only a link, or blank)
action_taken: Dropped
why: Nothing to score; keeping them would add fake neutral sentiment

problem_found: Google Trends writes very low interest as the text '<1'
action_taken: Replaced with 0.5 (the middle of 0–1) and cast the column to numbers
why: 0 would claim no searches at all; 1 overstates; 0.5 is the honest midpoint and too small to move any result

problem_found: Checked Trends files for missing days
action_taken: None missing across all 10 films — no fill needed
why: Each export covered every day of its window
